31:5.1.1.text: When the place sold, the old stuff went in the lot. Half the back rooms on the Fernberg have something of ours.

31:5.1.2.text: He paid for his bunk in quarters and fixed the dock for nothing. I'd have kept his gear forever.

31:5.2.1.text: Walt? He guided out of three places I know of. Never stayed. Good with the clients, didn't like the owners.

31:5.2.2.text: He'd go out alone in October. People said he was strange. I said he liked October.

31:5.3.1.text: Two pages. Page two's the wind. Nobody reads page two.

31:5.3.2.text: We overlapped two years, Wade and me. He kept his boots clean then too.

31:GY-01.1.text: Where did you get that tent.

31:GY-01.c1.text: Back room at {home}. They said nobody rents it.

31:GY-01.2.text: The back room. When the place sold, the old stuff went in the lot. Half the back rooms on the Fernberg have something of ours.

31:GY-01.3.text: Pipe ash. Two thousand five. He never patched it. Said it let the tent breathe.

31:GY-01.c3.text: It came with the pack. Why?

31:GY-01.4.text: Because it's not just a tent.

31:GY-01.5.text: Here. It went in the lot with everything else when the place sold. And it came back. Of course it came back.

31:GY-01.6.text: I'm Marlys. I do Tuesdays and Wednesdays. I used to do everything.

31:GY-01.7.text: Walt's. Walt Haapala. He bunked here the last two years. He paid for his bunk in quarters and fixed the dock for nothing. I'd have kept his gear forever.

31:GY-01.8.text: They found his canoe. That's what there is.

31:GY-01.9.text: I don't remember much about that week. It was a long time ago.

31:GY-01.c7.text: There was a notebook rolled in the fly.

31:GY-01.10.text: In the fly. I never unrolled it. I boxed it at six in the morning and I never— Keep it on you. Not in the pack. On you.
31:GY-01.10.if: Walt page: "Marlys boxed his things 'at six in the morning'. She doesn't remember that week."

31:GY-01.11.text: Go on. You've got a carry before dark.
31:GY-01.11.if: gives: Marlys met; Walt page: "Marlys, Moose Lake, Tuesdays and Wednesdays. She knew the tent by the burn hole."

31:GY-02.c1.if: needs: the nickname unmatched on the Walt page

31:GY-02.1.text: That's here. The bunkhouse. He said it was the room you wait in before you go in.

31:GY-02.2.text: Six bunks and a stove. Bunk three's by the window. He always took three. You could see his lamp from my kitchen.

31:GY-02.3.text: Third crib from the end. Every bolt in it's his. Gus doesn't know that and I don't tell him.

31:GY-02.4.text: 'Asking M. for a bunk he doesn't need.' That'd be me.

31:GY-02.c5.text: Who stayed in the bunkhouse that week?

31:GY-02.5.text: At the memorial I asked her if she wanted his things. She said she didn't want them in the house. I understood that better later than I did then.

31:GY-02.6.text: Somebody. A man. It was a long time ago.

31:GY-02.7.text: You know who. You've seen his boots.

31:GY-03.1.text: Sit, if you're going to stand there.

31:GY-03.2.text: You found his gear. Huh. Well. It's yours now, isn't it.

31:GY-03.3.text: Fifty years I know whose it was. That pack's been over Prairie more times than the tow boat.

31:GY-03.4.text: Walt? He guided out of three places I know of. Never stayed. Good with the clients, didn't like the owners.

31:GY-03.5.text: It is. Wind'll come up south by two. Don't trust a calm lake after two. That's Walt's pack.

31:GY-03.6.text: Hap Johnsrud. I guided off this dock from '58 to oh-two. Now I sit. My grandson brings me up so I can watch other people do it wrong.

31:GY-03.7.text: You want to know what Walt was like, you do a day with him. I can't. My legs are in Ely. So I'll give you the day, and you go do it, and you tell me what's there now.

31:GY-04.1.text: Bring that back. It's the only one.

31:GY-05.c1.text: New boards. The cribs are old.

31:GY-05.1.text: Third crib from the end's ours. Walt and me, spring of '86, for a case of beer the owner never paid. Walt fixed it again the last years, for his bunk. Marlys told me. He never said.

31:GY-05.2.text: The tow still drop you on the left as you come up?
31:GY-05.2.if: needs: been at the Sucker end of P194, **or** asked Rick or Nate where the tow lands

31:GY-05.c2.text: It's on the right now. By the start of the carry.
31:GY-05.c2.if: gentle: the "now" lets him keep the past

31:GY-05.3.text: On the right. Is it. Then it always was, and I've been putting it on the wrong side for forty years, and nobody said.

31:GY-05.c3.text: Walt knew. He let you have it.
31:GY-05.c3.if: only if GY-N2 has been read

31:GY-05.4.text: Did he. That's Walt. That's exactly Walt. He'd let you be wrong ten years if it didn't sink anybody.

31:GY-05.5.text: Walt never said. Walt never said a lot of things.

31:GY-05.c5.text: It was never on the left, Hap.

31:GY-05.6.text: Wasn't it. Well. That's what happens.

31:GY-05.7.text: Nate says you were right about Prairie. On the right. Sit down.

31:GY-05.c6.if: letting him have it, as Walt did

31:GY-05.8.text: Good. Good, I had that one, anyway.

31:GY-05.9.text: It's on the right, Grandpa. It's been on the right since I was born.

31:GY-05.10.text: Is it. You let me have it. Walt used to do that. All right. Sit down.

31:GY-05.11.text: Hundred and twenty-two in '58, and it'll be a hundred and twenty-two when they bury me. Walt said a hundred and twenty-one. Never more than a rod off, and mostly dead on. When he was off, it was the map's fault.

31:GY-05.c8.text: Lilacs out. And a stone step.

31:GY-05.12.text: His grandmother's. The government bought it, and the family burned it on the ice the winter of '65 rather than watch somebody else do it. Walt was eighteen. He didn't watch. Went to a dance in town and came home at three. Only time I ever knew him to dance. Lilacs are June. Go in June. His sister'd want a picture of those lilacs. Don't tell her I said so.
31:GY-05.12.if: lead: Aili, S7. Rings nothing new: Gus already has the shore.

31:GY-05.c10.text: Two walleye. South wind, like you said.

31:GY-05.13.text: They're there. They were there in '58. They'll be there when the lake isn't.

31:GY-05.14.text: South wind? No? There you go.

31:GY-06.1.text: I asked him that once. He said 'The far end,' like I was slow. Past Bald Eagle there's Gull. Nothing past Gull but Pietro, and he never once said Pietro.

31:GY-06.c2.if: needs: Eino's name, from Tauno or Ollie

31:GY-06.2.text: Eino. You know about that, then.

31:GY-06.3.text: Because you did my day. And because nobody asked. The sheriff never asked me one thing, and I was his oldest friend still breathing.

31:GY-06.4.text: That's enough. Nate's got the truck running.

31:GY-06b.c2.text: You were trying to keep him safe.

31:GY-06b.1.text: That's what I tell myself. Most days it works.

31:GY-06b.c3.text: He let it go. Then he didn't.

31:GY-06c.1.text: That's not one of his I know. Ask somebody who tripped with him.

31:GY-07.2.text: '99. I was on the water that day. Different lake. The sky went a colour I've got no word for.

31:GY-07.3.text: Rock's still there. Same as me. Sitting. Thank you.

31:GY-07.4.text: Hair jigs. I tied those the winter after I quit. Never fished one. Walt said they were too pretty to get wet. Get them wet.

31:GY-08.1.text: You're the one Hap's got doing his day. He's got everybody doing his day. Nobody's got it right yet.

31:GY-08.2.text: I was fourteen. Cut off his feet. Walt said it was the best picture anybody ever took of Hap, because of the feet.

31:GY-08.3.text: Three summers, '86 to '89. Carried, cleaned fish, kept my mouth shut. He paid me out of his own pocket on top of what the store paid. Never said it was him.

31:GY-08.c3.text: Where does the tow land at Prairie?

31:GY-08.4.text: On the right, by the start of the carry. Always has. Don't tell Hap. Hap's had it on the left since the Nixon years.

31:GY-08.5.text: Coffee before clients. Clients before fish. Fish before you.

31:GY-08.6.text: Hook it, hand them the rod, never say. That's the whole job. Took me twenty years to learn the 'never say'.

31:GY-08.7.text: Read the wind before you read the map.

31:GY-08.8.text: Never mark a client's map. They'll come back without you.

31:GY-08.9.text: Bring them all home. The fish are extra.

31:GY-08.10.text: Dad was at the plant thirty-one years and fished every weekend of it. If they do it right, fine. Nobody up here's ever seen anybody do it right, so. Ask me after.

31:GY-08.c6.text: Did Walt ever buy a canoe off anybody?
31:GY-08.c6.if: needs: the Walt page already says "went north"

31:GY-08.c7.text: He'd have needed a second one.

31:GY-08.12.text: September of '19 he came out to my place in Babbitt. Asked me did I know anybody with an old fifteen-foot aluminium. Somebody who wouldn't remember him. Said it was for a kid at the bunkhouse who couldn't afford a boat.

31:GY-08.13.text: There's a fella outside Eveleth, yard full of old boats. Cash, no names. I told him that. Never did see that kid.

31:GY-08.14.text: Huh. I never told anybody where to buy a canoe. You hear me?
31:GY-08.14.if: gives: Walt page, under things that don't add up: "Rick sent Walt to a man with a yard of old boats, September 2019. An old fifteen-foot aluminium, 'for a kid at the bunkhouse'." If NB83 has been read: "Sept 28. 'Off a fella on the Range, cash.' That's the one." **This never counts toward the "went north" turn**, because it only opens after. From now on Rick lies about it to anyone, including the player if asked again.

31:GY-09.1.text: You're not overdue, are you? Good. Nobody's overdue today.

31:GY-09.2.text: Volunteers. Mostly we find people who are fine and embarrassed. A canoe on a rock, a party on the wrong lake. Once in a while it's not that.

31:GY-09.3.text: Thirty-two years, Lake County. Retired in '22. They let me keep the boat. Well. They let me drive it.

31:GY-09.4.text: Ten days. Sonar at the canoe, the Beaver twice, every outfitter boat on the chain that first weekend. Nothing. On Birch you don't always find them. It's deep and it's cold.

31:GY-09.5.text: I wrote it up. Two pages. Page two's the wind. Nobody reads page two.

31:GY-09.6.text: Would you. What was the wind doing that night?

31:GY-09.11.text: I keep one here. Don't ask me why.

31:GY-09.c9.text: Who decided it was an accident?

31:GY-09.12.text: Somebody told the office it was an old man in a high wind. Somebody who used to work there. Everybody nodded.

31:GY-09.13.text: I'm not going to say a name on a dock.

31:GY-09b.1.text: Ollie taught me the drag line. 1991. He told me once about a canoe on the wrong shore, back in '77. I thought it was an old man's story. Same words.

31:GY-09b.2.text: Ollie walks the Stuart Portage evenings, Tuesdays and Thursdays. He'll say 'Evening' at you twice before he says anything else. Ask him about '77. Or don't.
31:GY-09b.2.if: lead: S1; Gus rings the Stuart Portage.

31:GY-10.1.text: Party of four out of here, due yesterday. Basswood. Wind's been north since Tuesday. They're probably sitting on a rock eating the last of the trail mix. Probably.

31:GY-10.2.text: A party with sense is tucked in on the calm side of something, out of it. A party without sense is on the downwind shore with a canoe full of water. Look at the calm sides first.

31:GY-10.3.text: I'll take the boat up the chain. You take the bay. Squad pays thirty out of the coffee can.

31:GY-10.4.text: We were going to wait one more day and then panic.

31:GY-10.5.text: Is it bad that we were kind of having fun?

31:GY-10.6.text: Good. They were where the wind said. That's what I should have done in '19. Gone and looked where the wind said. I wrote it down instead.
31:GY-10.6.if: gives: $30 on the trip-end screen; Sheila's trust. If GY-09 hasn't happened, her "Walt's search" topic now opens with that line.

31:GY-11.1.text: Wind's supposed to go south after dark {day}. If you wanted to see something for yourself. I can't make you, and I won't ask why. Landing at nine. Bring your light.

31:GY-11.2.text: Night runs? Twice a summer. Somebody's always a day late.

31:GY-11.3.text: I'm giving a canoeist a ride. That's all this is.

31:GY-11.4.text: Take the spare. You're not swamping your own boat for my curiosity. Swamp it out there. His was full. I'll be here. Don't make me come looking.

31:GY-12.1.text: There'd be a register. Every bunk, every night, in my hand. When Gus bought the place he threw out everything in the office. Not the registers. I put them up in the boathouse loft before he could.

31:GY-12.2.text: Ladder's on the left inside the door. Third rung's loose. It's been loose since 1998.

31:GY-12.3.text: Hip. Mice. And I didn't want to be up there with it by myself, if you want the truth.

31:GY-12.4.text: It's dry, and Gus is afraid of the ladder.

31:GY-12.5.text: Two W.H.s in the bunkhouse that week. Walt, bunk 3, from the 14th. W. Helstrom, day use, on the 15th.

31:GY-12.6.text: A message for Walt at 6:05 on the 17th: 'your friend called'. A Duluth number.

31:GY-12.c4.text: The number on Marlys's message is Denny's.

31:GY-12.c5.text: Marlys doesn't remember much about that week. She kept the message.

31:GY-12.7.text: swamped no paddle no foul play
31:GY-12.7.when: *the 2019 clipping, beside the 1977 one if held (bible 5.5

31:GY-13.1.text: Not here. Stay the night in three. I'll tell it as it went. Be down there before six.

31:GY-13.2.text: Three's paid for. It's been paid for since 2019.

31:GY-13.3.text: Because in the daytime it comes out like a story. It wasn't a story.

31:GY-13.4.text: Light that, would you. He always had it lit. You could see it from my kitchen.

31:GY-13.5.text: He always had it there. You could see it from my kitchen.

31:GY-13.6.text: Somebody wanting to know are the leeches in.

31:GY-13.7.text: I don't know. A nice voice. Older. Not from here.

31:GY-13.8.text: He went up and used the store phone. I didn't listen. I heard him say 'all week'. That's all I heard. I have to close. Gus counts the till like it's church.

31:GY-13.9.text: I locked up at ten. Same as tonight. Went to bed like it was any Thursday. I'll sit out here a while. I don't sleep much anymore.

31:GY-13.10.text: At one I got up for water, and there was a truck in the lot with the engine running and the lights off. I thought, hunters. It was October. Everybody's a hunter in October.

31:GY-13.11.text: You went and looked. Good. I didn't.

31:GY-13.12.text: You saw that one. You didn't go look either. Nobody does.

31:GY-13.13.text: That. You can't mistake this door, it's stuck since 1990. At two I heard it. Then the truck went. I lay there and told myself that was Walt going out early. I wanted it to be.

31:GY-13.14.text: Go to sleep. I'll be on the cot in the back room. Gus knows.

31:GY-13.15.text: You put it out. He didn't.

31:GY-13.16.text: At six I came down to start the coffee. His lamp was still burning. The battery was nearly gone. Bunk three was empty and his canoe was off the rack.

31:GY-13.17.text: I didn't call anybody. I should have called somebody. I put his pack and his tent in a box and put the box on the high shelf in the back, behind the winter stock. Where I slept last night. I don't know why.

31:GY-13.c7.text: Tell Sheila. She'll write it down.

31:GY-13.19.text: Sheila. She'd write it down. She writes everything down. Then I'd better tell it right.

31:GY-13.20.text: We overlapped two years, Wade and me.

31:GY-13.21.text: Wade Helstrom. The man in the coat. He's the one told the office 'old man, high wind'. He kept his boots clean then too.

31:GY-13.22.text: He kept his boots clean then too.

31:GY-13.23.text: That's what the sheriff said. It was good advice. It's kept me up for seven years. Take it, then. Somebody should have it that isn't me.
31:GY-13.23.if: no flag. Nothing is lost: the player keeps the register and the message either way. The county never reviews 2019.

31:GY-13.c11.text: I swamped a canoe mid-Birch in his wind. It went north. Every time.

31:GY-13.24.text: Then the box was the right thing.

31:GY-14.c1.text: What the wind did on Birch.

31:GY-14.c2.text: I swamped a canoe mid-Birch in his wind. It went north. Every time.

31:GY-14.1.text: Then the box was the right thing.

31:GY-15.2.text: That's him. That's the one who asked.

31:GY-17.1.text: Second from the left, back row. He hated that hat. His girl made him wear it. June. He married her three years later. She taught at Tower. Smartest person in any room he was in.

31:GY-17.2.text: Fall Lake outfit's long gone. The photo came with the wall.

31:GY-18.1.text: Walt did. Counter man here, Tuesdays to Saturdays, seven years. He paced every carry in our reach and wrote it on there. Said the printed ones were for people who didn't walk them. I can't bring myself to paint over it.

31:10.1.text: I don't remember much about that week.

31:10.2.text: I never told anybody where to buy a canoe.

31:10.4.text: I'm not going to say a name on a dock.

31:12.2.1.text: Gus said ask first. I didn't.

31:12.2.2.text: They read page two. Out loud, in a room. Took seven years.

31:12.2.3.text: He hooked it and handed you the rod. Never said a word. That's guiding. And they put me up there next to him. With hair.

31:12.2.4.text: I boxed his things so nobody could sell them.
